definitions.explanation: Extending or prolonging a person's life, especially through medical intervention. Also used figuratively for extending the lifespan of organizations, systems, or objects.

examples.japanese: {延命|えんめい}{治療|ちりょう}を{続|つづ}けるべきか。
{延命|えんめい}{措置|そち}について{家族|かぞく}で{話|はな}し{合|あ}った。
{老朽化|ろうきゅうか}した{橋|はし}の{延命|えんめい}{工事|こうじ}が{行|おこな}われ、あと20{年|ねん}は{使|つか}える{見通|みとお}しだ。
examples.english: Life-extension work was carried out on the aging bridge, and it is expected to last another 20 years.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in medical contexts as {延命|えんめい}{治療|ちりょう} (life-prolonging treatment) or {延命|えんめい}{措置|そち} (life-sustaining measures), which are frequently discussed in the context of end-of-life care and bioethics in Japan. Also used figuratively for infrastructure, equipment, and organizations: {建物|たてもの}の{延命|えんめい} (extending the life of a building).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {延命|えんめい}{治療|ちりょう}: life-prolonging treatment
- {延命|えんめい}{措置|そち}: life-sustaining measures
- {延命|えんめい}{工事|こうじ}: life-extension construction
- {延命|えんめい}を{図|はか}る: aim to extend the lifespan
